------------------------------------------
Ancient Hindu scriptures in Sanskrit, especially the वेदस्, are difficult to understand because of their archaic language and recondite ritual system. A commentary written by scholars coming in the Vedic tradition will be very helpful in unravelling their mysteries.
Skandasvāmin is the earliest of the commentators on the Ṛgveda known to us now, and whose commentary—though incomplete as extant now—is available. He was the son of one Bhartṛdhruva and belonged to the country of Valabhī (the modern Gujarat). He was the गुरु of Harisvāmin, the well-known commentator of Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. He might have lived around A.

.
His commentary is quite lucid. Apart from mentioning the ṛṣi (the sage who discovered the मन्त्र) and devatā (the deity to whom the मन्त्र is dedicated) he also deals with the grammatical factors involved and quotes several verses from other sources like the Anukramaṇīs (index-works). His opinion is that the Vedic mantras are meant to be used in sacrifices.
He has also written a commentary on the Nirukta of यास्क (800 B. C.).
See also ṚGVEDA.

Skambha
------------------------------------------
The Atharvaveda Saṁhitā (10.7) uses this word to indicate the Highest Being beyond even ब्रह्मा. Literally it means One who is the support and basis of the whole universe.
See also ATHARVAVEDA.

Skāndapurāṇa
------------------------------------------
It is one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas and the biggest of them all. It is available in two forms, the first having seven khaṇḍas and the second divided into six saṁhitās. The former has been fully available in print whereas only the first three of the latter are available.
The number of ślokas in the various editions varies from 81,000 up to 100,000.
The printed edition of the former contains 81,000 verses spread over 1671 chapters.
Since it is a very voluminous work, only a brief summary can be attempted here:
1. Māheśvarakhaṇḍa
Introduction; greatness of स्कन्द; story of Dakṣayajña and its destruction; fruits of worshipping the शिवलिङ्ग; story of Devendra; समुद्रमथन (churning of milky ocean to get अमृत or nectar); story of पार्वती and her मर्रिअगे to शिव; birth of कुमार (Skanda or षण्मुख or कार्त्तिकेय or सुब्रह्मण्य; कुमार’s fighting with तारकासुर and killing him; greatness of वासुदेव; story of the Pāṇḍavas; descriptions of several places of पिल्ग्रिमगे.
2. Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa
Story of वराहावतार (Boar-इन्चर्नतिओन्) rescuing भूदेवी or मोथेर् Earth; story of Kamalā and श्रीनिवास or वेङ्कटेश; legends of भरद्वाज and मार्कण्डेय; greatness (eulogy) of पुरुषोत्तम of पुरी; अम्बरीष’s episode; other episodes such as those of इन्द्र-dyumna, जैमिनि, नारद, and नीलकण्ठ; description of नरसिṁह; passage to ब्रह्मलोक; details concerning the rathayātra of Jagannātha of पुरी; story of दक्षिणामूर्ति; Daśavatāras; greatness of Badarī (place of पिल्ग्रिमगे); about some rituals and the method of observing एकादशी; importance of Bhāgavata; sacredness of the months Kārttika and Māgha (October-November and January-February).
3. Brahmakhaṇḍa
This khaṇḍa deals mainly with the following places of पिल्ग्रिमगे: Setu (Dhanuṣkoṭi); चक्रतीर्थ (near Rāmeśvara); Brahmakuṇḍa (near गया); रामतीर्थ (near गया); Lakṣmītīrtha (on the banks of गोदावरी river); Śaṅkhatīrtha (in Kururkṣetra).
Greatness of Rāmanātha शिव of रामेश्वरम्; philosophical principles; method of going on a पिल्ग्रिमगे; on the four varṇas and āśramas; on temples; धर्म as described in the smṛtis; eulogy of दान (gifts); duties of a vaiṣṇava.
Greatness of शिव and his पञ्चाक्षरी मन्त्र (namaś-śivāya); sacredness of गोकर्ण (place of पिल्ग्रिमगे dedicated to शिव) and the शिवरात्रि festival; on the rudrākṣi beads.
4. Kāśīkhaṇḍa
Stories of pativratās (wives devoted to their husbands); the सप्तर्षिस् (the Seven Great Sages); story of ध्रुव; description of तपोलोक; eulogy of वाराणसी; story of the deliverance of a devil.
5. Avantīkhaṇḍa
Story of the महाकाल forest; a beautiful hymn of शिव; the vratas (reli-gious observances) of नागपञ्चमी and गौरी; description of some more pilgrim centres; story of the king

. Nāgarakhaṇḍa
Manifestation of शिव as the शिव-लिङ्ग; story of the king हरिश्चन्द्र; विश्वामित्र’s extraordinary feats including sending the king त्रिशङ्कु to हेअवेन्; greatness of Hāṭakeśvara (on the bank of the गोदावरी); other centres like विष्णु-pāda (Gayā), गोकर्ण, वाराणसी, द्वारका, Avantī and वृन्दाबन्; description of sacred rivers गङ्गा, नर्मदा and सरस्वती.
7. Prabhāsakhaṇḍa
Several legends connected with some ancient personalities like Someśa, Viśveśa, Siddheśvara, Narakeśvara, Saṁvarteśa and Nidhīśvara.
See also PURĀṆAS.
